question: cairn/devices/trouble's charter says only the RECIPIENT clears a trouble, and only by naming what changed. Who is the recipient — is it a RECORDED FIELD on the trouble, or an inference a reader makes? For the two live troubles (the-runtime-spine-has-never-run, workflow-cursor-unreadable-by-the-chokepoint), name them.
whats_beyond: Law 6 needs exactly one owner and needs it recorded, not inferred — a clear-gate that cannot say who may clear cannot refuse anyone. This is the load-bearing half of the alarms work: the DISPLAY half is the part most likely to be waste, because both live troubles have been printed in the session-open banner at every single session open and are still live. Being unseen is not their problem. The clear path has three requirements written in trouble's charter — identify the recipient, refuse a clear that names no change, write through trouble's own door rather than to the files — and none of the three is measured as existing today.
